6: This was a challenging question with few candidates understanding the concept of a computer model. Many believed that it was an actual model bridge and composed their answers accordingly. Correct answers generally centred around the concepts of safety and costs. Even though these candidates gained marks for these answers few candidates were able to explain why these were important. For the prose questions candidates need to give reasons or expansions to their answers in order to achieve good marks.
7: This was a very challenging question for most candidates especially in part (a) which was a new topic for the examination. (a) Extended reality is a mixture of virtual reality and augmented reality. Few candidates gained marks on this question as they described virtual reality rather than extended reality. (b) This topic had been set previous and candidates then were able to gain good marks, however candidates found this question was more challenging than in previous examination series. Candidates knew what a 3D printer was and how it operated but could not relate this to industrial processes and the reasons that 3D printers were a good idea or a bad idea. Some candidates wrote that 3D printers worked faster than a human carrying out the task and that they could work all night. However, candidates could have gained marks by stating that if there had been a power outage or a fault in the programming then no one would know until it was too late. There was a misconception that 3D printers produced perfect models but did not add that it depended on the program. Some candidates correctly stated that the 3D printer could only work with some materials and that they produced fewer parts, and their initial cost could be high. This was one of the harder questions on the paper and candidates had to analyse the use of 3D printers giving both positives and negatives.
8: Most of this question was quite challenging for the candidates, with only part (b) gaining good marks. (a) This was a challenging question with candidates explaining the concepts concerned with the internet working or not and this affecting the smart security system. Some candidates thought that if the internet connection failed then the system would go off, rather than the owner not being able to monitor it. (b) There were some good answers to this question with the concepts of sensors used in a security system being understood by most candidates. (c) This question which was related to the ANPR system was generally well understood and some good answers were seen. Some candidates did not fully read the question and thought the system had to do with road safety. Some candidates however thought that the CCTV camera was in some way the intelligent body and did not envisage any connected computer system or database. (d) Some sensible problems that could occur to stop the number plate being read were seen. However with some of the answers seen this session some candidates do not give the full explanation or reasoning behind their answers. For example some candidates rightly stated that ‘it may confuse numbers and letters’ without explaining why this would be the case. Others stated that the number plate could not be reads if it was dirty or the weather conditions were bad without expanding on the answers given.
